description: A particle chased across a one or two dimensional field: the incoming signal gives a target position, the particle is accelerated towards it, and the output is where the particle got to

params.text: Sets how hard the particle is pulled towards the target, over about eighteen octaves of pull
Sets how much of its speed the particle keeps from one sample to the next, none at the far left
Sets how far from the target the particle has to be before it is pulled at all; inside this distance it coasts
Sets how much speed the particle keeps when it strikes the wall, none at the far left and almost all at the far right
Sets how much of the acceleration jack reaches the acceleration, inverted anticlockwise of centre and none at centre
Sets how much of the friction jack reaches the friction, inverted anticlockwise of centre and none at centre
Sets how much of the distance jack reaches the trigger distance, inverted anticlockwise of centre and none at centre
Sets how much of the bounce jack reaches the bounce, inverted anticlockwise of centre and none at centre
Sets how much of the drive jack reaches the drive, inverted anticlockwise of centre and none at centre
Sets how much of the shake jack is added to the particle's speed, inverted anticlockwise of centre and none at centre
Multiplies the incoming signal on the way in and divides the outgoing one by the same amount, so the particle is worked harder against the same walls
Scales the acceleration and the trigger distance for the signal being tracked: the upper position is set up for audio and the lower divides both down for control voltages
Chooses how the speed is bled away: in the lower position a fixed amount is taken off each sample, and in the upper position a fixed proportion of it
Chooses whether the two input jacks are read as X and Y positions or as a radius and an angle
Sets how many times the motion is worked out per sample, 1 to 16; higher settings keep fast signals stable and cost more processing

inputs.text: Shifts the acceleration by one doubling per volt at the far ends of the attenuverter above it
Shifts the friction, scaled by the attenuverter above it and divided by ten
Shifts the trigger distance, scaled by the attenuverter above it and halved
Shifts the bounce, scaled by the attenuverter above it and divided by ten
Shifts the drive, scaled by the attenuverter above it and halved
Adds directly to the particle's speed, which knocks it off course without moving the target
The target position along the first axis, read as X in rectangular coordinates and as the radius in polar; patching this jack alone puts the module into one dimensional mode
The target position along the second axis, read as Y in rectangular coordinates and as the angle in polar; patching this jack puts the module into two dimensional mode

outputs.text: The particle's position along the first axis, squashed through a hyperbolic tangent and scaled by 12
The particle's position along the second axis; it is held at 0V in one dimensional mode
The particle's speed, as a positive voltage, which rises as the particle is thrown about and settles as it catches up with the target

notes: The mode is chosen by what is patched, not by a switch: the second axis jack makes it two dimensional, the first axis or the shake jack alone makes it one dimensional
With all three of those jacks empty both position outputs are held at 0V
The wall the particle bounces off is ten units from the centre; the maker's manual gives twelve, which is the number the outputs are scaled by rather than where the wall is
The boundary is a circle in two dimensional mode whichever coordinate system is chosen; there is no square boundary in the code
menu: Use Classic Theme — returns the panel to the original untinted artwork, which no entry in the Panel Theme list will give back
